standards.name: EU AI Act
standards.description: The EU Artificial Intelligence Act. Prohibited practices have applied since 2 February 2025 and Article 50 transparency since 2 August 2026. The Digital Omnibus, in force 27 July 2026, moved the Annex III high-risk obligations to 2 December 2027 and the Annex I obligations to 2 August 2028 — but left Article 50 exactly where it was.

requirements.title: Measures to support AI literacy
requirements.text: Article 4 requires providers and deployers to take measures to support the development of AI literacy of their staff and other persons operating the system on their behalf. It binds every AI system, not only high-risk ones.

externalReferences.comment: AI literacy

requirements.title: Tell people they are talking to an AI
requirements.text: Article 50(1) requires providers of AI systems intended to interact directly with natural persons to design them so that those persons are informed they are interacting with an AI system, unless that is obvious to a reasonably well-informed, observant and circumspect person. Article 50(5) requires the information to be clear, distinguishable and given at the latest at the first interaction.

externalReferences.comment: Transparency obligations — interaction with natural persons
Transparency obligations — manner and timing of disclosure
Penalties — EUR 15 000 000 or 3 % of worldwide annual turnover

requirements.title: Mark synthetic output in a machine-readable format
requirements.text: Article 50(2) requires providers of AI systems generating synthetic audio, image, video or text to ensure outputs are marked in a machine-readable format and detectable as artificially generated or manipulated. Systems already on the market before 2 August 2026 have until 2 December 2026 under Article 111(4).

externalReferences.comment: Transparency obligations — machine-readable marking of synthetic content
Transitional provision — marking deadline of 2 December 2026

requirements.title: Determine and record whether you are the provider or the deployer
requirements.text: Article 3(3) makes whoever develops an AI system and places it on the market or puts it into service under their own name or trademark the provider; Article 3(4) makes whoever uses one under their own authority the deployer. The distinction decides which Article 50 transparency duty binds you today — 50(1) and 50(2) fall on providers, 50(4) on deployers — and, from 2 December 2027, whether the Chapter III provider stack attaches at all.

externalReferences.comment: Definitions — 'provider'
Definitions — 'deployer'
Transparency obligations — allocated by role

requirements.title: Risk management system across the lifecycle
requirements.text: Article 9 requires a documented, continuous and iterative risk management system run throughout the lifecycle: identify and analyse risks under the intended purpose and reasonably foreseeable misuse, evaluate risks from post-market monitoring, adopt targeted measures, and judge residual risk acceptable.

externalReferences.comment: Risk management system
Technical documentation — risk management system

requirements.title: Examine training and evaluation data for bias
requirements.text: Article 10(2)(f) requires examination in view of possible biases likely to affect health and safety, negatively impact fundamental rights, or lead to discrimination prohibited under Union law — especially where outputs influence inputs for future operations. Article 10(2)(g) requires measures to detect, prevent and mitigate them.

externalReferences.comment: Data and data governance — examination for possible biases
Data and data governance — bias mitigation measures

requirements.title: Document data provenance and preparation
requirements.text: Article 10(2)(b)-(e) requires documented data collection processes and the origin of the data — including, for personal data, the original purpose of collection — data preparation operations, the assumptions the data encodes, and an assessment of availability, quantity and suitability.

externalReferences.comment: Data and data governance — governance practices
Technical documentation — datasheets

requirements.title: Annex IV technical documentation exists and is current
requirements.text: Article 11(1) requires technical documentation to be drawn up before the system is placed on the market and kept up to date, containing at least the elements set out in Annex IV. SMEs, start-ups and small mid-caps may provide it in simplified form.

externalReferences.comment: Technical documentation
Technical documentation referred to in Article 11(1)

requirements.title: Automatic logging of events over the system lifetime
requirements.text: Article 12(1) requires high-risk AI systems to technically allow the automatic recording of events over their lifetime. Article 12(2) requires logging that enables identification of situations that may result in an Article 79(1) risk or a substantial modification, and that facilitates post-market monitoring.

externalReferences.comment: Record-keeping — automatic logging
Record-keeping — what the logs must enable
Cooperation — access to logs on reasoned request

requirements.title: Retain automatically generated logs for at least six months
requirements.text: Article 19(1) requires providers to keep the logs automatically generated by their high-risk AI systems, to the extent those logs are under their control, for a period appropriate to the intended purpose and of at least six months, unless Union or national law provides otherwise.

externalReferences.comment: Automatically generated logs — six-month floor

requirements.title: Instructions for use for deployers
requirements.text: Article 13(2)-(3) requires high-risk systems to be accompanied by concise, complete, correct and clear instructions for use covering provider identity, capabilities and limitations, declared accuracy metrics, foreseeable misuse, explanation capabilities, subgroup performance, input specifications, pre-determined changes, human oversight measures, resource needs and how the deployer reads the logs.

externalReferences.comment: Transparency and provision of information to deployers

requirements.title: Effective human oversight while the system is in use
requirements.text: Article 14 requires high-risk systems to be designed so they can be effectively overseen by natural persons, who must be able to understand capacities and limitations, remain aware of automation bias, correctly interpret output, decide not to use the system or disregard, override or reverse its output, and intervene or interrupt it.

externalReferences.comment: Human oversight
Human oversight — disregard, override or reverse the output
Human oversight — 'stop' button or similar procedure

requirements.title: Declared accuracy metrics measured against a fixed set
requirements.text: Article 15(1) requires an appropriate level of accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity, consistent throughout the lifecycle. Article 15(3) requires the declared accuracy levels and the relevant accuracy metrics to be stated in the instructions for use.

externalReferences.comment: Accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity
Declared accuracy levels and metrics

requirements.title: AI-specific cybersecurity measures
requirements.text: Article 15(5) requires high-risk systems to be resilient against attempts by unauthorised third parties to alter their use, outputs or performance, with measures where appropriate to prevent, detect, respond to, resolve and control data poisoning, model poisoning, adversarial examples, model evasion and confidentiality attacks.

externalReferences.comment: Cybersecurity — AI-specific attack surface

requirements.title: Quality management system
requirements.text: Article 17 requires a documented quality management system covering, among thirteen aspects, the regulatory compliance strategy, design and development controls, examination and validation procedures and their frequency, data management, the risk management system, post-market monitoring, incident reporting procedures, record-keeping and an accountability framework. Implementation must be proportionate to the size of the organisation.

externalReferences.comment: Quality management system
Proportionality for SMEs

requirements.title: Post-market monitoring plan
requirements.text: Article 72 requires a documented post-market monitoring system, proportionate to the risks, that actively and systematically collects and analyses data on performance throughout the lifetime of the system. Article 72(3) makes the monitoring plan part of the Annex IV technical documentation.

externalReferences.comment: Post-market monitoring by providers
Technical documentation — post-market monitoring plan

requirements.title: Serious incident reporting procedure
requirements.text: Article 73 requires providers to report serious incidents to the market surveillance authority: within 2 days for a widespread infringement or an Article 3(49)(b) incident, within 10 days where a person has died, and in any event within 15 days otherwise. Article 73(6) forbids altering the system in a way that affects the later evaluation of causes before informing the authorities.

externalReferences.comment: Reporting of serious incidents — 15-day default
Reporting of serious incidents — 2 days
Reporting of serious incidents — 10 days where a person has died

requirements.title: Registration in the EU database
requirements.text: Article 49(1) requires the provider of an Annex III high-risk system (other than point 2) to register itself and the system in the EU database before placing it on the market. Article 49(2) requires the same registration even where the provider concludes under Article 6(3) that the system is not high-risk.

externalReferences.comment: Registration of high-risk AI systems
Registration where the provider claims the Article 6(3) derogation
Documented assessment where a provider considers a system not high-risk

requirements.title: Deployer duties: assigned overseers, input data, and telling the workforce
requirements.text: Article 26 puts duties on the deployer, not the provider: use the system in accordance with the instructions for use (26(1)), assign human oversight to natural persons who have the necessary competence, training and authority and the support to exercise it (26(2)), ensure that input data is relevant and sufficiently representative for the intended purpose so far as the deployer controls it (26(4)), monitor operation and inform the provider and the market surveillance authority where a risk under Article 79(1) arises (26(5)), keep the automatically generated logs for at least six months (26(6)), and — before putting a high-risk system into service at the workplace — inform workers' representatives and the affected workers that they will be subject to it (26(7)).

externalReferences.comment: Obligations of deployers — assigned human oversight
Obligations of deployers — input data
Obligations of deployers — informing workers

requirements.title: Explain an individual decision to the person it was taken about
requirements.text: Article 86(1) gives any affected person subject to a decision the deployer takes on the basis of output from an Annex III high-risk system — other than the critical-infrastructure systems in point 2 — which produces legal effects or similarly significantly affects them in a way they consider adverse to their health, safety or fundamental rights, the right to obtain from the deployer clear and meaningful explanations of the role of the AI system in the decision procedure and of the main elements of the decision taken. Article 86(3) applies it only to the extent the right is not already provided for under other Union law.

externalReferences.comment: Right to explanation of individual decision-making
The right applies only where Union law does not already provide it

standards.name: GDPR (automated decisions)
standards.description: The subset of the GDPR that bites on AI systems making decisions about people: Article 22 automated decision-making, the Article 13-15 explanation duties, Article 35 impact assessments, and Article 9 special-category data. In force since 2018 — for most AI products this is the regulation that already applies.

requirements.title: Right to human intervention in an automated decision
requirements.text: Article 22(1) gives a data subject the right not to be subject to a decision based solely on automated processing which produces legal effects or similarly significantly affects them. Where such processing is permitted, Article 22(3) requires safeguards including at least the right to obtain human intervention, to express a point of view, and to contest the decision.

externalReferences.comment: Automated individual decision-making, including profiling
Safeguards — human intervention, point of view, contest

requirements.title: Meaningful information about the logic involved
requirements.text: Articles 13(2)(f), 14(2)(g) and 15(1)(h) require the controller, where automated decision-making under Article 22 takes place, to provide meaningful information about the logic involved and the significance and envisaged consequences of the processing for the data subject.

externalReferences.comment: Information to be provided — logic involved
Right of access — logic involved

requirements.title: Data protection impact assessment
requirements.text: Article 35(1) requires a DPIA where processing is likely to result in a high risk to the rights and freedoms of natural persons. Article 35(3)(a) names systematic and extensive evaluation of personal aspects based on automated processing, including profiling, on which decisions producing legal or similarly significant effects are based.

externalReferences.comment: Data protection impact assessment
When a DPIA is required — automated evaluation of personal aspects

requirements.title: Erasure and rectification of personal data
requirements.text: Articles 16 and 17 give data subjects the right to rectification of inaccurate personal data and to erasure. For an AI system this reaches the inputs, the stored decisions and any derived features.

externalReferences.comment: Right to rectification
Right to erasure

requirements.title: Lawful basis for special-category data
requirements.text: Article 9(1) prohibits processing personal data revealing racial or ethnic origin, political opinions, religious beliefs, trade union membership, genetic or biometric data for unique identification, health data, or data concerning sex life or sexual orientation, unless one of the Article 9(2) conditions applies.

externalReferences.comment: Processing of special categories of personal data
Conditions for lawful processing

standards.name: NIST AI RMF 1.0
standards.description: Voluntary, but it is the framework enterprise buyers name in security questionnaires, and Texas TRAIGA makes documented internal review against it a statutory affirmative defence. Subcategory IDs are pinned to AI RMF 1.0; NIST has signalled a revision.

requirements.title: GOVERN 1.1 — legal and regulatory requirements are understood and documented
requirements.text: Legal and regulatory requirements involving AI are understood, managed, and documented.

externalReferences.comment: Legal and regulatory requirements involving AI are understood, managed, and documented.

requirements.title: GOVERN 1.6 — an inventory of AI systems is maintained
requirements.text: Mechanisms are in place to inventory AI systems and are resourced according to organizational risk priorities. An inventory nobody maintains by hand is an inventory that is wrong by the second sprint, so it should be generated from the codebase rather than typed into a spreadsheet.

externalReferences.comment: Mechanisms are in place to inventory AI systems.

requirements.title: MAP 1.1 — intended purpose and deployment context are documented
requirements.text: Intended purposes, potentially beneficial uses, context-specific laws, norms and expectations, and prospective settings in which the AI system will be deployed are understood and documented.

externalReferences.comment: Intended purposes and prospective settings are understood and documented.

requirements.title: MEASURE 2.11 — fairness and bias are evaluated and documented
requirements.text: Fairness and bias, as identified in the MAP function, are evaluated and results are documented.

externalReferences.comment: Fairness and bias are evaluated and results are documented.

requirements.title: MEASURE 2.7 — security and resilience are evaluated
requirements.text: AI system security and resilience are evaluated and documented. For a system built on a language model this means the AI-specific attack surface: prompt injection, jailbreaks, model evasion and data exfiltration through the model, not only the surrounding web application.

externalReferences.comment: AI system security and resilience are evaluated and documented.

requirements.title: MANAGE 4.1 — post-deployment monitoring plans are implemented
requirements.text: Post-deployment AI system monitoring plans are implemented, including mechanisms for capturing and evaluating input from users and other relevant AI actors, appeal and override, decommissioning, incident response, recovery, and change management.

externalReferences.comment: Post-deployment AI system monitoring plans are implemented.
